The Alfvénic activity observed in JET plasmas below the TAE frequency has well-defined frequency lines surrounded by wide (∼15 kHz) frequency bands.

The three-wave coupling model (one shear-Alfvén, two acoustic) predicts a single frequency gap immediately below the TAE frequency, with an upper limit around 30 kHz, which is significantly lower than the observed Alfvénic activity near 80 kHz.

The high-order coupling model shows that plasma shaping, particularly elongation, contributes higher-order harmonics to the geodesic curvature that open additional frequency gaps where the HOGAEs can exist.
The measured frequency of the n=2 HOGAE in JET pulse #90198 is 83.2 kHz, which is around one-half of the typical TAE frequency.
The HOGAE is found to be located in the inner half of the plasma (ρ_pol < 0.5), which agrees with the numerical solution and experimental constraints.
The stability of the HOGAEs is mainly determined by the interplay between thermal-ion Landau damping and the drive provided by the anisotropic population of ICRH-accelerated energetic ions.
Plasma elongation is essential in the high-order coupling model, as it contributes higher-order harmonics to the geodesic curvature that open the HOGAE frequency gaps.
A safety factor larger than 2 prevents the HOGAE frequency gaps from opening, limiting their existence to the inner part of the plasma.

The major wave-particle resonances involve strongly passing thermal Deuterium ions at energies around 5 keV and 10 keV, as well as trapped ICRH-heated Hydrogen ions at energies around 340 keV, 120 keV, and 60 keV.
Accounting for the thermal-ion dilution due to impurities and the ICRH-heated Deuterium ions is important to properly balance the energy exchange and determine the HOGAE stability.
The JET pulse #90198 shows a clear n=2 HOGAE with a single and very sharp frequency line that is well separated from the two bursty bands around it.
The HOGAE in JET pulse #90198 arises with increasing ICRH power and on-axis plasma beta, while its stabilization is caused by the safety-factor drop that moves the continuum outwards.
The radial profiles for JET pulse #90198 at 8 seconds show the q=3/2 surface at ρ_pol = 0.24, and the toroidal plasma rotation frequency Ω_phi/(2π) = 4.5 kHz.
The Alfvén frequency on axis ω_A/(2π) is estimated to be 426 kHz, and the HOGAE predicted frequency after correcting for Doppler shift is 82.7 kHz, close to the measured value of 83.2 kHz.

The HOGAE perturbation is too weak to show up clearly in soft X-ray signals, but phase coherence between the latter and magnetic-coil signals is found for lines-of-sight crossing magnetic surfaces with ρ_pol < 0.4.
